articles.headline: Altman: Cavs built for 'sustainable run' despite missing on LeBron
articles.description: Cavs president of basketball operations Koby Altman said he wasn't fazed when LeBron James chose to sign with the Sixers, saying, "We're built for a sustainable run here regardless of one outcome."
articles.body:
INDEPENDENCE, Ohio -- Koby Altman would have loved for LeBron James to return for a third stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers.

When the most popular player in franchise history decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, the Cavaliers' president of basketball operations wasn't fazed.

"We can't be reliant on one outcome. I think we have too much of a good thing going in terms of our infrastructure, our foundation to worry about one outcome," Altman said at a news conference Friday before the Cavaliers begin training camp next week. "I'm not downplaying the enormity and magnitude of the decision. I just think the way we're built as an organization is we have a great foundation and a great sort of ecosystem in terms of talent, coaching staff, our performance staff and we're built for a sustainable run here regardless of one outcome."

James' agent, Rich Paul, said on his podcast in July that the Cavaliers were the only team to meet with James, while Miami and Golden State were the other finalists.

Altman has been able to build a contending roster since James' second departure in 2018 after he led the Cavs to four straight trips to the NBA Finals and the franchise's first championship in 2016.

Cleveland has won at least 50 games the past two years and reached the Eastern Conference finals last season for the first time since 2018. The team was swept in four games by the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks.

The Cavs quickly pivoted after James' decision and addressed their need for a wing player, acquiring Peyton Watson in a five-team trade and signing him to a four-year, $88 million contract. On the first day of free agency, Donovan Mitchell signed a four-year, $273 million contract extension.

James Harden, who was acquired near the trade deadline, signed a three-year, $97 million extension that gave the Cavaliers some flexibility under the salary cap by going below both aprons.

"You go through the list and zoom out and say, 'OK, was this offseason a success? Were we able to get better? Did we look at the future? Did we get more financial flexibility, more sustainability with the roster?' All of those things lead me to say this was a really good offseason in spite of that one decision," Altman said.

While the 37-year-old Harden and 30-year-old Mitchell are the team leaders, the 24-year-old Watson gives the Cavs another young player who can mesh with Evan Mobley (25), Jarrett Allen (28) and Jaylon Tyson (23).

Watson started a career-high 40 games last season with the Denver Nuggets and averaged career bests in points (14.6), rebounds (4.9) and assists (2.1).

"What I've been seeing in the gym is the defense, first of all. And then he shot 41% from 3 last year. It's a one-year sample, but there's a lot of room for growth in his offensive game, especially the way we play," coach Kenny Atkinson said.

articles.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley to be 'fearless' vs. Bears despite stinger
articles.description: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley plans to play "fearless" Monday night against the Chicago Bears as he eyes a return from a stinger injury.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのセイクワン・バークリー、神経損傷を抱えながらもベアーズ戦で「恐れずに」プレーへ
articles.descriptionJa: イーグルスのランニングバック、セイクワン・バークリーは、神経損傷（スティンガー）からの復帰を目指し、月曜夜のシカゴ・ベアーズ戦で「恐れずに」プレーする意向を示しています。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley plans to play "fearless" Monday night against the Chicago Bears as he eyes a return from a stinger injury.

Barkley was tackled for no gain by defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on the first offensive snap from scrimmage and went indoors after being examined in the medical tent.

He returned briefly in the second half but played just 10 of a possible 72 snaps and finished with four carries for 9 yards.

Barkley returned to the practice field this week after undergoing an MRI on Monday. He was listed as a full participant Friday after being limited Thursday.

"I've had a history of [stingers] before. This is the first bad one I had in a long time," he said. "It's also like a wake-up call to me. I've been super active focusing on my lower body and longevity of my career. I probably wasn't as great as I needed to be with my neck stability and strengthening my neck. So it's putting that within my routine and having that as part of my process and kind of the same way I attack everything from head to toe, do the same thing with my neck.

"It's good to have an MRI knowing it's nothing, hopefully, God willing, where I worry about my career and I can just go out there and play free."

Barkley, 29, returned to the game Sunday with a neck roll and plans to wear a modified version Monday night that allows for greater mobility.

Barkley has rushed for 92 yards on 19 carries through two games this season (4.8 yards per carry). He has not missed a full game due to injury in his two-plus years in Philadelphia.

"I don't think so," Barkley said, when asked if the injury will affect him against Chicago. "That's why I'm rehabbing my ass off, to get it as strong as it needs to be. I feel like I'm in a really good spot. I know they wouldn't let me go out there if I wasn't able to do it.

"I'm going to let the game come, and I'm going to go out there and play fearless, don't worry about."

Manchester United are keeping tabs on Club Brugge left back Joaquin Seys, while Barcelona attacking midfielder Dani Olmo is on the radar of Bayern Munich. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

The German giants are preparing contingency plans amid growing interest from rival clubs in Jamal Musiala and Michael Olise, and have maintained a long-term interest in the 28-year-old that dates back to his time at RB Leipzig. Olmo, who won the World Cup with Spain this summer, has a transfer valuation estimated at €70 million and could be offloaded as Barcelona look to build funds to sign Julián Álvarez from Atlético Madrid.

However, Bournemouth are reported to be looking for a fee of at least £100 million.

But there is also interest from Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United, Sunderland, and Everton.

The Senegal international is now also being tracked by Liverpool.

articles.headline: Hornets star Kon Knueppel sidelined with hamstring injury
articles.description: The Charlotte Hornets will be without Kon Knueppel for at least the entire preseason due to a left hamstring injury, the team announced Friday.
articles.headlineJa: ホーネッツのスター、コン・クニューペルがハムストリングの負傷で離脱
articles.descriptionJa: シャーロット・ホーネッツは、コン・クニューペルが左ハムストリングの負傷のため、少なくともプレシーズン全期間を欠場することを金曜日に発表しました。
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets will be without Kon Knueppel for at least the entire preseason due to a left hamstring injury, the team announced Friday.

Knueppel, who was the first rookie to lead the league with 273 made 3-pointers last season, suffered the hamstring injury during offseason on-court activity, the team said. Veteran forward Grant Williams also injured his right hamstring.

 

The Hornets have ruled both players out for all four of Charlotte's preseason games. They will be reevaluated "during the first week of the regular season," according to the team.

Charlotte opens the season at Brooklyn on Oct. 21.

The Hornets are hoping to rely even more on Knueppel this season after trading LaMelo Ball to Minnesota over the summer. Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 42.5% 3-point shooting as a rookie.

Williams has averaged 7.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game during his seven seasons.

articles.headline: QB Sam Darnold back Sunday, but Seahawks down two safeties
articles.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.
articles.headlineJa: QBサム・ダーノルドが日曜日に復帰、しかしシーホークスはセーフティ2名を欠く
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのクォーターバック、サム・ダーノルドが日曜日に先発出場しますが、前年スーパーボウル王者のチームはジュリアン・ラブとタイ・オカダの両先発セーフティが欠場となりました。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday against the Washington Commanders, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.

Backup defensive tackle Brandon Pili (concussion/neck) is questionable. No other Seahawks player has a game designation.

Darnold missed most of the first two games with a glute injury he suffered early in the season opener. He was limited Wednesday in his return to practice and was a full participant Thursday and Friday. Coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Darnold looked "really good" this week.

 

"Sam's going to play, and he's ready to go," Macdonald said. "He's done a great job."

Speaking with reporters Thursday, Darnold said he briefly feared that his season might be over -- and that his career could be impacted long term -- when he was hurt on the fifth play of Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. After backup Drew Lock led Seattle to a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals and a 2-0 start last week, Macdonald said Darnold's timetable had "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Macdonald was asked Friday what he needed to see from Darnold this week.

"Really just to see him confident in the things that he's been doing," Macdonald said. "He's been really positive and says he feels great. He looks great, so we'll rolling. It's a medical miracle he's back."

Rodney Thomas II will make his third straight start for Okada, who remains out with a hamstring injury. Macdonald said AJ Finley will start for Love, who popped up on the injury report as a nonparticipant Thursday when a calf tightened up. Love was again a nonparticipant Friday. Macdonald said he doesn't know how much time Love will miss.

Love has an interception in three straight games dating to Seattle's Super Bowl LX win over New England.

Finley will make his first start since entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Mississippi in 2023. Claimed off waivers from the Los Angeles Chargers in November 2024, Finley missed all of last season after tearing an ACL in the team's annual training camp practice at Lumen Field. After intercepting Darnold during the same event this summer, Finley acknowledged how meaningful it was to him, calling it a "full-circle moment."

"You're really bummed about Julian obviously because he's had such a great start to the season and he's such a great player," Macdonald said. "But when AJ got the pick in training camp, I'm thinking about the journey he's been on over the last year and the way he's really gotten his body back and his movement. He had a great practice today. He's on it. He's sharp as a whip, great communication, ball skills, all those things. So I'm excited for him to have the opportunity."

Okada is still unable to practice.

articles.headline: Commanders rule RG Cosmi, TE Okonkwo, LB Luvu out Sunday
articles.description: Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) won't play Sunday vs. the Seahawks.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズ、RGコスミ、TEオコンクウォ、LBルブの日曜日の欠場を発表
articles.descriptionJa: ライトガードのサム・コスミ（脳振盪）、タイトエンドのチグ・オコンクウォ（ハムストリング）、ラインバッカーのフランキー・ルブ（股関節）は、日曜日のシーホークス戦に出場しません。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders ruled out three starters for Sunday's game against the visiting Seattle Seahawks, further depleting their roster.

Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) won't play, according to the game status report released Friday.

Washington (0-2) already was without quarterback Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow) and safety Nick Cross (internal injury).

 

Luvu and Okonkwo missed the 37-20 loss at Dallas in Week 2. The other three players were hurt vs. the Cowboys; Cross needed to stay overnight in a Dallas hospital.

Leo Chenal replaced Luvu in the starting lineup next to rookie Sonny Styles. Luvu was Washington's defensive playcaller, but Styles handled that in Week 2.

Cross will be difficult to replace because he lines up in a variety of positions, from linebacker in some packages to a box safety and deep safety. Quan Martin will replace him in the starting lineup. Coaches like Martin's versatility as well.

Okonkwo was signed in the offseason to provide explosive plays downfield. Without him, the team will use a rotation of John Bates, Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff. But the Commanders also like to use three-receiver sets. They've used that look 67.9% of the time through two games.

Cosmi suffered the concussion in the fourth quarter vs. Dallas. Washington could replace him by moving Nick Allegretti from center to guard, where he has started the bulk of his career, and inserting veteran Lucas Patrick at center. The Commanders could start veteran Andrew Wylie at guard as well.

Washington has lost 12 of its past 14 games dating to last season. The Commanders lost their opener at Philadelphia 24-22. They still have four players on injured reserve, including projected starting cornerback Trey Amos (ankle). The others are linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), defensive end Deatrich Wise Jr. (quad) and running back Jeremy McNichols (quad).

The good news for Washington is that Daniels is expected to return soon from his dislocated left elbow, though it's uncertain how many games he will miss.
